players.product: GEM 63 / GEM 63XL solid rocket boosters for the Atlas V and Vulcan launch vehicles

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 2026 sales accelerated to $10.9 billion, up 10% sequentially and 5% year-over-year, with growth in all four segments; segment operating income decreased slightly versus the prior year (Q2 2025 benefited from a $76 million favorable Sentinel EAC adjustment); diluted EPS was $7.68, helped by a lower effective tax rate (remeasurement of uncertain tax positions) and a gain on the sale of an equity investment.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 sales $10.9 billion; +5% YoY; +10% sequential; EPS $7.68

quarterly_data.signal: CEO/CFO: Q2 2026 net awards were $20 billion, a book-to-bill ratio of 1.84 times, driving backlog up 17% year-over-year to a record $105 billion; CEO expects continued strong bookings for the rest of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: $20 billion awards; book-to-bill 1.84 times; backlog $105 billion (+17% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO/CFO: raised 2026 guidance - sales $43.75 billion-$44.25 billion ($44 billion midpoint, over 5% organic growth per the CEO); mark-to-market adjusted EPS $28.60-$29.10 (raised $1.20); full-year book-to-bill now at least 1.25 times; segment operating income outlook reaffirmed; adjusted free cash flow $3.1 billion-$3.5 billion reaffirmed (includes several hundred million dollars expected this year from the B-21 asset sale); CFO anticipates mid to high single-digit year-over-year sales growth in Q3 and an effective tax rate of mid 14%.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 sales $43.75 billion-$44.25 billion; EPS $28.60-$29.10; FCF $3.1 billion-$3.5 billion; book-to-bill at least 1.25

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 capital expenditures were $302 million and continued to ramp to expand facilities for customer demand; Northrop still expects $1.85 billion of capex in 2026 and capex of around 4.5% of sales in 2027 and 2028 to support the B-21 production ramp. Q2 adjusted free cash flow was nearly $1 billion; operating cash flows increased about 30% from 2023 through the current year. CFO: a view on 2027-2028 free cash flow will be given in Q3, updated in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex $302 million; 2026 capex $1.85 billion; ~4.5% of sales in 2027-2028

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Space segment Q2 sales rose 4%, driven by higher volume on NASA's Commercial Resupply Services mission and missile defense programs; Q2 operating margin was 8.6%, including an unfavorable EAC adjustment on GEM 63XL for higher estimated cost and quantity of materials; the rest of Space earned over 11%. 2026 Space sales still about $11 billion with a significant second-half increase (national security space volume, new awards, improved GEM 63XL performance); margin expectation lowered to the low 10% range.
quarterly_data.figure: Space Q2 sales +4%; margin 8.6%; 2026 Space sales ~$11 billion; margin low 10%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: on GEM 63XL Northrop progressed the root-cause investigation of the anomaly on a launch in Q1 and is implementing corrective actions, including a component redesign now proven in a successful static fire test; it expects to begin delivering the redesigned motors by the end of the year; the added work and material are reflected in the updated EAC.
quarterly_data.figure: redesigned GEM 63XL motor deliveries expected by the end of the year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: national security space backlog stands at over $16 billion (programs like GPI, GWS and restricted efforts); for 2026 the national security space business is projected to grow high single digits to over $7 billion in sales, more than 15% of company revenue, driven by space security, space resilience and missile defense. In Q&A the CEO said the area grows double digit toward about 15% of revenue and that Northrop has a growing pipeline outside the U.S. for its space portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: NSS backlog over $16 billion; 2026 NSS sales over $7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Northrop's first Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV), a commercial robotic spacecraft with two robotic arms to repair, relocate and service satellites in geosynchronous orbit and install life-extension jetpacks (prolonging satellite life up to eight years), was scheduled to launch later on the day of the call, weather permitting; Northrop invested under a commercial model and expects it to become operational in 2027 as part of its service offerings for commercial and government clients. The CEO describes it as the first commercial robotic spacecraft of its kind (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: first MRV scheduled to launch on the call day (weather permitting); operational in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: NASA is moving away from its original Gateway plans; Northrop is restructuring the HALO contract so the technology contributes to NASA's future Gateway plans, which will reduce revenue this year but extend it over a longer period.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: further Sentinel definitization and authorization with the Air Force added $7.6 billion to program backlog; Q2 contract incentives improved profitability; an acoustic test of the Sentinel missile was completed, with first flight of the integrated missile expected in 2027; solid rocket motors for the first five flight tests are in production; Northrop broke ground on another facility at its Utah campus (adding to 1.1 million square feet purpose-built for Sentinel) to support the production phase starting later this decade.
quarterly_data.figure: $7.6 billion Sentinel backlog increase; first flight expected 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Northrop completed qualification to become a solid rocket motor supplier on PAC-3 and reached a $2 billion framework agreement with the Department of Defense and Lockheed Martin; it expects the PAC-3 SRM production award later this year (definitized as FY2027 appropriations fund it) and is starting to build ahead of the definitized contract. As a brand-new supplier it will start at a smaller scale that grows over time (quantities not disclosed).
quarterly_data.figure: $2 billion framework agreement
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: framework agreement party (PAC-3 solid rocket motors)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Northrop has 10 multi-year agreements for missile acceleration in work across the portfolio, with up to $10 billion of sales opportunity over the next seven years; price and fee negotiations are ahead and contracts are to be definitized as funding becomes available, this year and probably into early next.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 multi-year agreements; up to $10 billion over seven years

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Aeronautics Systems Q2 sales rose 13% (higher volumes on B-21, TACAMO and mature production programs) with a 10.3% margin; 2026 AS sales raised to approximately $14 billion and margin to the mid-to-high 9% range. CEO: the agreement reached with the Air Force allows the Air Force to consider accelerating B-21 production into a larger program of record; the Air Force analysis is under way, with a conclusion expected by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: AS Q2 sales +13%; margin 10.3%; 2026 AS sales ~$14 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Defense Systems Q2 sales rose 5% (7% organic) on the Sentinel and missile defense ramp; margin 7.5% including a $68 million unfavorable adjustment on SiAW (11% excluding it); DS backlog nearly $35 billion. 2026 DS outlook maintained at mid-to-high $8 billion sales and about 10% margin, with second-half revenue up more than $700 million (ammunition, weapons timing, Sentinel, IBCS) and second-half margin over 11%.
quarterly_data.figure: DS Q2 sales +5% (7% organic); margin 7.5%; $68 million SiAW charge; backlog nearly $35 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: higher projected costs to complete qualification testing on the Stand-in Attack Weapon (SiAW, U.S. Air Force) stem from ARRW testing delays; with AARGM-Extended Range for the Navy it forms Northrop's tactical missile strategy, and GEM 63XL and SiAW each represent billions of dollars of potential sales at accretive margins over the next decade (CEO); qualification is not done, so risk remains.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Mission Systems Q2 sales rose 3% (marine programs, F-35 sensors, restricted airborne radar) with margin improved to 15.4%; 2026 MS sales guidance kept at high $12 billion, margin raised to approximately 15%, with a second-half sequential sales increase of more than $600 million; intersegment eliminations about $2.7 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: MS Q2 sales +3%; margin 15.4%; 2026 MS sales high $12 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: microelectronics growth has been lower this year, particularly in restricted microelectronics, after growing very strongly last year; the chips are vertically integrated into Northrop's MS, space, aeronautics and DS products and also sold to other customers for secure processing; underlying demand is still robust and expected to increase over time.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Northrop targets doubling annual international sales to $10 billion by 2031. Kuwait received State Department authorization in May for six IBCS systems (order announced in Q2); UAE and Qatar have sent letters of request for IBCS, with discussions in other Middle East countries; NATO allies made a commitment for the Triton autonomous aircraft and NATO has expressed interest in buying up to five Tritons, with Northrop working with NATO through the rest of the year to get on contract next; Northrop was selected to establish an in-country solid rocket motor manufacturing facility in Australia; FMS cases are being approved much faster than in prior years.
quarterly_data.figure: international sales target $10 billion by 2031; six IBCS systems for Kuwait; up to five Tritons

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Golden Dome reconciliation dollars, slow early in the year, opened up in Q2 and are being put onto contract; Northrop expects more selection decisions and contract actions through the rest of the year and into early next, and revenue from Golden Dome-related activity to continue to scale. On space-based AMTI/GMTI the CEO said Northrop has capability and is looking at future tranches of requirements, without bid decisions yet.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: nuclear-navy propulsion modernization is the biggest growth driver of the marine business, now out of development and delivering its first low-rate initial production units, expected to scale through this and the next decade.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Northrop's programs are well supported in the U.S. base budget and 2027 growth does not depend on significant supplemental funding; she declined to quantify 2027 growth but cited book-to-bill of 1.25, double-digit international growth and a margin tailwind as the mix shifts from development to production; company margins were nearing high 11s excluding the two EAC adjustments (GEM 63XL, SiAW).
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure
